item.title: the case for refactoring
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Every few months refactoring bites me again. This is what finally stuck.

why it matters

Refactoring shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • If it is hard to test, that is the design telling you something.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.
  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: on refactoring
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
I keep coming back to refactoring, so here are the notes I wish I had earlier.

why it matters

Refactoring shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Prefer the obvious solution; clever costs interest forever.
  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

item.title: a small guide to refactoring
item.author: Brenner Cruvinel
item.description:
Short post: refactoring is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Refactoring shows up across programming work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • If it is hard to test, that is the design telling you something.
  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.
  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
